rules.proteins: The species has no curated record of its machines, so each machine's proteins are looked for by family. Each part of the machine in the Human dossier has its narrowest InterPro families (entries of the type Family under which no other Family entry of the same protein lies); a protein of the species whose signatures include one of them is a candidate for that part ('candidate by family'). A candidate is never called the part or a counterpart: a family says what a protein is like, not what it does in this cell. No protein is matched by a name. A protein's signatures are its line's own and the InterPro entries that the species' own scan (InterProScan 5.78-109.0, data/proteins/planarian/interproscan.json) found on it and its line lacks (data/proteins/planarian/interproscan_added.tsv). Those count as carried by the line, but the highest entry that each group of lines carries is read from the table's own column alone. A family that no line carries is 'not in the table' where every group of lines was scanned, in its own column, at a release that knew it, or where a database that the scan ran on every protein of the table has a signature in it; otherwise the nearest broader Family that some line carries is used, or the table cannot tell.
rules.structure: The species' own entries are found by a search of the Protein Data Bank by its taxon alone; one is used where it holds candidates for at least half of the parts that have candidates, and for at least two parts where the reference's machine has two or more, ranked as the reference dossier ranks. Otherwise the machine has no structure of its own ('None in hand'), and the reference dossier's entry is named under structure_elsewhere, with its organism.
rules.join: Each candidate is a line of the atlas's own table (data/proteins/planarian/predicted_proteins.tsv) by its id. by_protein gives, for each of them, the machines it is a candidate of.
